prompt:
Below is a policy summary from a UK general election manifesto. Identify the party that produced it. You must choose one.

<text>
# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Overview
The manifesto addresses the cost of living crisis, climate change, and public service reform, presenting policy proposals across multiple sectors.

## Healthcare
The party proposes £28bn additional annual NHS funding by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability (£3bn annually by 2030), boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. They oppose NHS privatisation and support the NHS Reinstatement Bill. Mental health services would receive investment for 28-day therapy access, with counsellors in all schools.

## Social Care
Proposals include free personal care (similar to Scotland's model), £20bn annual investment, improved carer pay and career structures, and ending exploitation of overseas care workers.

## Housing
The party proposes 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and a £29bn five-year home insulation programme targeting EPC B standards.

## Energy
Plans include wind power providing 70% of electricity by 2030, no new fossil fuel licences, ending oil and gas subsidies, community energy ownership, and opposing new nuclear development. A carbon tax starting at £120/tonne, rising to £500/tonne, would be introduced.

## Economy
The manifesto proposes £40bn average annual green investment, bringing railways, water companies and major energy retailers into public ownership, a £15/hour minimum wage, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, and repealing anti-union legislation.

## Taxation
Proposals include a wealth tax (1% above £10m assets, 2% above £1bn), aligning capital gains with income tax rates, reforming inheritance tax, and a carbon tax estimated to raise £80bn annually by parliament's end.

## Welfare
Plans include £40/week Universal Credit increase, abolishing the two-child benefit cap, 5% disability benefit increase, ending the five-week benefit wait, and scrapping the bedroom tax.

## Environment
Proposals include a Rights of Nature Act giving legal personhood to nature, protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, public water ownership, and Right to Roam legislation.

## Education
The party proposes £8bn school investment, £5bn for SEND provision, scrapping tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, free school meals, and moving academies to local authority control.

## Transport
Plans include £10bn annual public transport subsidies, railway renationalisation, local bus control, £2.5bn annual cycling/walking investment, free bus travel for under-18s, ending petrol/diesel vehicle sales by 2027, and a frequent flyer levy.

## Democracy
Proposals include proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and repealing the Elections Act 2022.

## Immigration
The party proposes ending the hostile environment policy, creating safe asylum routes, allowing asylum seekers to work during applications, and removing minimum income requirements for spousal visas.

## Foreign Policy
Positions include calling for an Israel-Gaza ceasefire, recognising Palestine, increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI by 2033, working toward EU rejoining, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while cancelling Trident.

## Funding
The manifesto estimates raising £50-70bn annually through tax reforms by parliament's end, with additional borrowing for capital investment. Total revenue spending would reach £161.6bn by 2030, with capital spending of £90.3bn.
</text>
